messages:
maya: Heads-up — planning an interruption rehearsal for mixed-capacity GPU pools next Tue 09:00 PT. Goal: validate graceful fallback to reserved/dedicated without SLO loss, and ensure cost controls don’t blow up. Who's in?
kevin: +1. Can we scope to one tenant (alpha) + platform traffic only? keep blast radius tiny.
sara: SG. Recommend targeting one nodepool in us-west1-a (mixed: 70% preemptible, 30% on-demand). We should also exercise zone fallback to us-west1-b.
raj: I'll own the eviction script and pod drain automation. Plan to force terminate preemptible VMs via cloud API, then observe autoscaler + rollout.
tom: I can simulate burst requests from the canary loadgen and add latency probes. Need to know the exact success criteria.
maya: Success criteria draft: 1) 99.9% request success for alpha within 5m window; 2) p95 latency must stay <300ms, p99 <800ms; 3) autoscaler restores target replica count within 90s for steady-state; 4) No rollback to older model versions; 5) Cost spike during event < +10% vs baseline. Thoughts?
kevin: Add: no manual ops required to failover OOM/eviction cases (i.e., automation handles it). And alerts should auto-annotate the run id.
sara: Also capture KV-cache warmup time — if we fallback to a quantized variant, we need to measure quality/regression in the evaluation harness.
raj: Eviction approach: run https://cloud.example.com/api/terminate?pool=alpha&count=20 to kill 20% of preemptibles over 30s, then another 30% after 2m. Will post the script in the repo.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled interruption-rehearsal:eng-infra:1768501234 created. Run ID: ir-2026-03-25-0900. Tags: mixed-pool, low-blast.
tom: Runbook checklist (quick):
```
- freeze prod deploys to alpha 08:30-10:30 PT
- snapshot dashboards + perf baselines at 08:45
- enable replication to dedicated pool before 08:50
- run termination stage 1 (20%) at 09:00
- monitor autoscaler, rollout, queue depths
- run termination stage 2 (30%) at 09:03
- simulate request spike at 09:05
- verify metrics + post-mortem notes by 09:30
```
kevin: We should toggle batching off for one run to validate token cost per request under pressure. Add as a variant: run A = normal batching, run B = forced small-batch.
sara: I'll prepare evals for outputs and quality regression tests; will run synthetic prompt set before/after. Need model hashes to pin.
maya: Ops: please ensure SLO page and alerts are suppressed to avoid paging the oncall unless it crosses customer-impact threshold. ops-oncall, aware?
ops-oncall: Aware. Pager suppression window set for run ID ir-2026-03-25-0900. Critical pages remain. I'll join the channel live.
raj: Posting termination snippet (GCP example):
```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  'https://cloud.example.com/api/terminate?pool=alpha&percent=20'
```
We also have a k8s drain helper: `./tools/drain-with-retry.sh --grace 60` to avoid noisy restarts.
sara: Reminder: after failover, we need to validate KV cache hit rate; if hit rate < 60% we may see token cost blowouts. Capture before/after histograms.
kevin: I'll instrument a cost guard that kills the interruption if 10m burn-rate exceeds 15% over baseline — do we want that?
maya: Yes — safety cutoff in infra-bot. infra-bot, can we abort run automatically on burn-rate?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: ack. Automation: abort-on-cost-threshold=15pct enabled. Will stop further termination stages if triggered.
tom: Logistics: post the meeting link and zoom ops bridge. I'll also record the dashboard moments.
raj: Assignments:
- raj: termination scripts + drain helper (PR by EOD Fri)
- sara: eval harness + KV-cache checks + model pins (PR by Mon)
- kevin: cost guard + batching toggle flags (PR by Mon)
- tom: loadgen scenarios + recording (PR by Mon)
- maya: run coordination + postmortem template (PR by Mon)
ops-oncall: I'll monitor and un-suppress if customer impact detected.
maya: Thanks all — will post final checklist + run id in #eng-infra tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
